summary: Implement Ruling W1 (OWNER-DIRECTIVES-2026-08-14.md §6): an aggregate may never be the binding predicate for something a player meets one at a time. Five predicates tightened per BAR-AUDIT-WORLD-20260814 §5.1-§5.6, the world re-measured against them, and the corpus swept for the same shape.
next_step: ARM B OF RI-WLD15 IS STILL OWED and NEEDS A SCOPING RULING. RI-WLD15/RI-WLD16 stay `not_run`. Corrected arithmetic: the full M-W15-2 protocol is 6 transects x 13 regions x 90 frames = 7,020 frames, which at the capture service's published 21.9 s/frame cold is 42.7 HOURS of exclusive browser - not affordable on any box. (My first estimate of ~6 h was wrong; corrected in reports/RULING-W1-REMEASURE.md rather than quietly edited.) RECOMMENDED, ruled not asked: run the worst-2-regions variant first - `node corpus/80-methods/m-wld15-armb.mjs --regions deep-marshes,valus-ridge --json <path>` - 360 frames, ~2.2 h, at the specified 8 m resolution so no threshold needs reinterpreting; those are the two regions arm A ranks worst (275 s and 312 s unchanging-ground runs). If they fail, the next step is all 13 regions at 2 transects and 24 m spacing (780 frames, ~4.7 h) and M-W15-2 should be rewritten around it. Re-runs on the same build are ~0.4 h warm. Run `--selfcheck` first; it is green and browser-free.
explicitly_not_touched: game/** — the job is the bar, not the world. W1-30F owns terrain and vegetation and consumes RI-WLD15/RI-WLD16; a separate visual programme is live in render and world source.
game/data/world/voids.json — the coordinate-frame defect found in §6 of the report is a world-data bug, reported and deliberately left for its owner.
game/data/world/hazards.json — needs an area_fraction/footprint field before M18's hazard axis can be measured; named, not added.

RI-WLD07 §5, RI-QST04, RI-WLD14, RI-DLG05 — the four sweep hits. Reported with exact proposed predicates, not edited: amending a live bar other pieces are judged against is an orchestrator's call, the same discipline the audit applied.
contention_note: node tools/contention.mjs returned GO at start (3 instances, 2.45/core), flipped to WAIT before arm B (load 4.4/core against a 4.0 ceiling), then cleared to GO again. I did NOT take a browser for the full arm B run: the protocol is 7,020 frames at ~21.9 s/frame cold = 42.7 hours of exclusive browser, which no box can give it (rule 21, and the arithmetic). One single-frame smoke test WAS taken through the shared capture daemon to prove the path works end to end: a real placed frame in the Deep Marshes, 640x360, 143.6 s cold including daemon boot.
findings: RI-WLD04 M18 — magnitude floors added to the four axes that had none (weather >=20 pp L1, audio >=50% of EACH bed, hazard >=15% areal occupancy, slope Cramer's V >=0.20 replacing a bare chi-square) plus RI-WLD16's compulsory landform axis folded in. Measured: 78/78 pairs passed the old form, 77/78 pass the new one. The floors were mostly ALREADY EARNED — minimum observed weather difference is 49.4 pp against a 20 pp floor, minimum audio difference 67% against 50%. The single failing pair is deep-marshes/western-rootlands, which shares both macro_form (levee-and-backswamp) and drainage (anastomosing); RI-WLD16 §1 permits the shared form only if drainage load separates them, and it does not yet.

The 20 pp weather floor was VERIFIED, not copied. All 36 Vvardenfell pairwise L1 distances recomputed from the census reproduce min 20 / median 90 / max 200; going back to the wikitext in the local UESP extract, Sheogorad (15/40/10/15/10/10) against West Gash (15/30/15/20/10/10) sums to 20 pp by hand and is genuinely the closest pair. The 0.727 place-type Jaccard ceiling reproduces too. Both recomputations now run inside --selfcheck so the figures cannot drift from the data silently.

A derivation the audit did not anticipate had to be designed: our 13 regions use 41 REGION-SPECIFIC weather state names, so comparing raw state sets puts nearly every pair 200 pp apart by construction and the axis would pass automatically — the same instrument-validity failure the ruling exists to stop, one level down. Morrowind's REGN records share an eight-word vocabulary, which is what makes 20 pp meaningful. States are therefore bucketed by light level and sightline band (what a player perceives) and the STATIONARY distributions compared. Recorded in RI-WLD04 M18 because changing it changes every number.

RI-WLD04 M19 — spread and reach clauses added (>=3 of 4 region quadrants, >=40% of region land within 400 m). 13/13 elements passed on count alone; 12/13 pass with spread. Valus Ridge's rock flutes are 14 instances in 2 of 4 quadrants.

RI-WLD07 §4 — the clearest case. Area-weighted world mean slope 10.07 deg sits comfortably in the 6-14 band and the old row passes, while the MEDIAN REGION is 5.32 deg, 7 of 13 regions are under 5.5 deg and only 4 of 13 are in band. Valus Ridge (30.28) and the Salt Hills (16.62) carry the average for everyone.

Implementing RI-WLD07 §4 to the audit's LETTER would have made the bar WEAKER. The audit proposed pointing the row at RI-WLD16 §3's class envelopes; all 13 regions already sit inside theirs, because those envelopes are deliberately wide (built to catch a playa modelled as a ridge, not to tune a slope). So the row now binds three ways: every region inside its class envelope (worst-constituent), median region >=6 deg (quantile), no region under 3 deg (worst-constituent hard floor). The quantile rather than the worst constituent is deliberate and is the ruling's own falsifier — binding every region to 6-14 deg would fail the Eastern Rootlands for being a tidal flat.

Two RI-WLD07 §4 rows were DEMOTED to descriptive rather than re-scoped: 'land below +5 m 35-50%' and 'land above +100 m >=12%' have no honest per-region form (every region in a coastal marsh is either almost all below 5 m or almost none). Their per-region job is done by the relief envelope. Saying so beats leaving two aggregate rows that look binding and are not.

RI-WLD02 — D14 (place-type Jaccard <=0.727 every region pair) and D15 (>=1 POI class unique to each region) added, anchored on Vvardenfell's own measured 0.267-0.727 spread and its eight single-region place types. Measured: 13 of 77 measurable pairs over the ceiling (three at 1.0), and 0 of 13 regions own a POI class. CONTEXT MATTERS: pois.json holds 42 POIs across 4 classes against a 1,060-POI target and DECLARES ITSELF INCOMPLETE, naming dungeon entrances, caves, shrines, signposts and stations as not yet placed. This is an early system, not a wrong one; what the rows add is that region character now has to be built in rather than retrofitted.

RI-WLD09 — V11 added (landscape variety unrelaxed inside void tracts; emptiness is authored, sameness is not), implementing RI-WLD15 M-W15-4, which the item had named since it was written and no instrument had ever implemented.

UNEXPECTED FINDING, and the most consequential one: all five declared void polygons in game/data/world/voids.json are in a DIFFERENT COORDINATE FRAME from terrain.json. V-01 is declared in the Deep Marshes with a polygon spanning x -940..-210 while the world runs x 0..4825 and the Deep Marshes sits at x 2472..3592. No single offset reconciles them (V-01 needs +3412 in x, V-02 needs -692). None of the five tracts can be located in the world. V1-V9 all pass regardless because every one reads a metadata field and none reads a position — the same shape as the failures this ruling is about, one layer down. It also silently disables RI-WLD02's 'outside declared void tracts' scoping for D1/D2/D13. New row V10 guards it. Nobody's blunder: voids.json has no runtime consumer in game/src, so there was never a moment it would have shown up in play.

SWEEP — all 147 reference items searched for predicates binding on a mean, total, or 'any difference' over a population met one at a time; 57 items produced 85 candidate lines, all read. FOUR CONFIRMED HITS: (1) RI-WLD07 §5 'mean interior floor area 40 m2 / 120 m2 / mean volume >=9,000 m3' — you open one door at a time, and 150 broom cupboards plus 10 halls average to 40 m2; the fail floors are means too. Strongest hit, three rows below the §4 I just fixed. (2) RI-QST04 scoring bands and a HARD FAIL on 'mean resolutions < 2.0' with no per-quest floor — you play one quest at a time. (3) RI-WLD14 E2 'distinct decay types across the province >=4' — four types in one city passes while twelve regions show one; identical in shape to the D15 gap just closed. (4) RI-DLG05 'mean time-to-find <=4 minutes', partly guarded by its 7/10 proportion. Proposed predicates are spelled out in the report; none was edited.

SWEEP — CLEARED, with reasons, because a sweep that reports only hits is not a sweep. The largest group of grep hits (8 lines across RI-AI05, RI-WLD10, RI-WLD13, RI-JRN03, RI-PLT01, RI-TRV01) is 'any difference' as a FAIL condition — determinism assertions, opposite polarity to the ruling. Frame-data 'active/total <= 0.16' rows are ratios within one animation, not aggregates over a population. Pixel- and frame-population means (RI-VIS02/03, RI-MAG05) are out of scope by construction. And several items are ALREADY in the correct form and worth copying: RI-WPN03 UNQ ('>=1 for EVERY weapon' plus a roster mean), RI-LOR01 ('min-over-axes, never the mean' — the ruling, written before the ruling), RI-WLD07 §5's own bonfire row ('<=6 min from ANY road point, median <=3'), RI-DLG02 §5 (a mean bounded by two tail requirements), RI-AI01 (99th percentile alongside the mean), RI-QST01 (monotonic mean with a stated >=2 effect size).

NULL CONTROLS caught four real defects before any number was published, which is the whole argument for the ruling's plausible-near-miss requirement. (1) The audio metric was WRONG: '>=50% of assets differ' implemented as Jaccard distance scores exactly 0.50 when one asset of three is swapped, so the audit's own named near-miss would have cleared the floor on a technicality; measuring the shared fraction against each bed's own size gives 0.33. (2) My first C control was toothless — it gave the flat regions landform classes that MATCHED their flat terrain, so it passed and proved nothing; rebuilt as seven flat regions DECLARING karst towers and escarpments. (3) The arm-B controls were the empty-world trap again: featureless gradient frames made the pHash pure noise; rebuilt with horizons, landmark silhouettes, props, forward motion and drifting light. (4) m-wld15-monotony.mjs ran its CLI at module load, so importing it exited the importer.

A slope-units trap avoided: terrain.json stores a per-region mean_slope_deg (world 10.07 deg) and a raster derivation from the 25 m base_dm channel gives systematically gentler numbers (world 8.28 deg), because the raster cannot express the sub-cell micro-relief the generator included. RI-WLD16 §3's envelopes, landforms.json's measured_* fields and m-wld16's L2 are all authored against the STORED field, so check C binds on that and reports the raster figure only as a cross-check. Judging a stored-slope envelope with a raster-derived slope would have failed regions for the units they were measured in.

ARM B COST is a finding in its own right: M-W15-2 as specified is 7,020 frames = 42.7 h of exclusive browser, which no box can give it. The item's protocol is not buildable as written and needs rescoping. I got this wrong at first (estimated ~6 h), caught it by recomputing, and corrected it in the report in place rather than silently. The instrument supports --regions so a worst-two-regions run at full 8 m resolution is 360 frames and ~2.2 h.
could_not_do: ARM B OF RI-WLD15 - not run. RI-WLD15 and RI-WLD16 remain not_run, correctly; arm A is a gate, not a verdict. The full protocol costs 42.7 h of exclusive browser (7,020 frames at 21.9 s/frame cold), so it is unaffordable as written and needs a scoping ruling - see next_step for the recommended 2.2 h variant. A single-frame smoke test through the shared capture daemon confirmed the path works end to end (a real placed frame in the Deep Marshes, 640x360, 143.6 s cold including daemon boot). The instrument is written and fully validated WITHOUT a browser, so the owed work is one command rather than a project.

The M18 hazard axis cannot be measured: hazards.json declares which regions a hazard applies to and nothing about how much ground it covers. Scored conservatively as not-differing on all 78 pairs — claiming an axis differs when its magnitude cannot be checked is exactly the habit the ruling forbids — and the item names the fix as a data change, not a bar change.
RI-WLD04 M17 (blind screenshot) and M20 (audio blind) were not run; both need a browser and fresh judges. Nothing in the report rests on them.

en.uesp.net is egress-blocked from this container (403 via curl, EGRESS_BLOCKED via WebFetch). Every Morrowind figure comes from the local 2019-11-07 UESP extract, which predates the ESO Blackwood chapter (2021).
The four sweep hits were reported, not repaired — other items' territory with pieces in flight against them.
notes: HAZARD, for successors: git index contention is severe. Mid-task another agent's bank committed my in-flight files AND reset the working tree, silently reverting several instrument fixes. It was caught only because a published figure (8.28 deg) did not match the one I had verified by hand (10.07 deg). bank.mjs itself timed out at 180 s (exit 143) and `git commit --only` hit repeated index.lock contention; the work landed anyway because another agent's bank swept it in. Verify your own files are in HEAD with `git show HEAD:<path> | grep <a string you added>` rather than trusting a commit to have happened.

No agent graded its own work here: the five replacements are the audit's, specified before this task existed; this task implemented and measured them. The instrument's controls are the check on the instrument.
All five reversals and falsifiers are written into the items themselves, per the ruling's reversibility requirement.
